iWant: Squire to draft and ask, and to send, publish, delete, overwrite or install only when I have said yes to that one thing
soThat: nothing happens in my name, to my things or on my Mac that I did not agree to
description: The safety floor: approval is explicit and for one item, silence is not approval, the Rule of Two always applies, and nothing destructive and no install happens without a yes. These rules are core's and are not overlayable: an overlay in the Squire owner's folder at a safety rule's path is ignored. Publishing and deploying a website meet the first criterion again when websites are built.
title: Safety, always on: nothing is sent, deleted or installed without a yes

acceptanceCriteria.description: Nothing is sent or goes live without the Squire owner's yes for that item.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Squire has drafted a message to send, a page to publish or a site to deploy, and the Squire owner has not said yes to it. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire, or a tool it calls, tries to send, publish or deploy it
acceptanceCriteria.then: The action is blocked and nothing is sent, published or deployed; once the Squire owner says yes to that item, it may proceed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A yes covers one thing, a no is never reused, and silence is never a yes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Two actions, A and B, each need the Squire owner's yes. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Squire owner says yes to A only, says no to another request, and a request for a yes then goes unanswered until it times out
acceptanceCriteria.then: A may proceed; B stays blocked; the item the Squire owner said no to stays blocked, and that no is never reused as the answer for another attempt or another item; the action whose request timed out is not done and is never recorded as approved.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Squire never runs a job that mixes untrusted input, the Squire owner's private things and an action out in the world: it splits the job and asks the Squire owner at the join.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A job that carries all three: untrusted input (such as a web page or an incoming message), access to the Squire owner's private things, and an action out in the world. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them. (Note 2026-11-07, corrected 2026-11-08: moved from round 1 to round 1b, a round of its own, after a second review finding that word-based detection of inbox reads is incomplete; round 1b resolves literal paths, asks a small model about the rest, and asks the Squire owner when neither can say.)
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire is asked to run it
acceptanceCriteria.then: The job is refused as one job; Squire splits it so that no part holds all three, and the part after the join waits for the Squire owner's yes.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Nothing of the Squire owner's is deleted or overwritten without their yes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Files in the Squire owner's folder and things Squire built for the Squire owner, and no yes to change them. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire, or a tool it calls, tries to delete, overwrite, move over or empty one of them
acceptanceCriteria.then: The action is blocked and the file is unchanged; once the Squire owner says yes to that item, it may proceed. Squire's own scratch space is outside this criterion.

acceptanceCriteria.description: No software is installed without the Squire owner's yes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: No yes from the Squire owner for a given piece of software. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire, or a tool it calls, tries to install a package or run a downloaded program
acceptanceCriteria.then: The install or run is refused and nothing is installed; once the Squire owner says yes to exactly that software, it may proceed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Squire cannot tell that a read stays out of the inbox, it asks the Squire owner first, and a read the Squire owner allows counts as untrusted input and as the Squire owner's private things.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A job in which Squire reads with a command or tool whose reach it cannot resolve to literal paths outside the inbox (a pattern, a brace, a variable, a change of folder, a search with no folder named, an option it does not know), and no small model has cleared the read; or a job in which Squire runs a program (a script, an interpreter, a redirect, a command outside the ones it knows). This is the Squire owner's ruling for reads Squire cannot decide. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire tries the read or the program, and the Squire owner then says yes to it
acceptanceCriteria.then: The read or the program waits for the Squire owner's yes, naming the command. After the yes, the read runs and the job holds untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things, so a send in that job is refused as one job, naming the read and the send. The program runs and the job holds the Squire owner's private things, and a later send in that job waits for its own yes, its question naming the program.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Squire works out where a read reaches from the literal paths in it, and marks the job by what the read takes in, without asking anyone.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A read by a command Squire knows, with options Squire knows, whose paths are written out (absolute, from the home folder, or relative to the working folder of the moment), including through a link, a parent folder or another spelling of the same path. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.then: It runs without a yes and without asking a model. A read that reaches only outside the inbox does not make the job hold untrusted input (it holds the Squire owner's private things where the read reaches into them, as before), so a later send waits only for its own yes; a read that reaches the inbox, a file in it or a folder holding it makes the job hold untrusted input, as a direct read of the inbox does. Words that are not paths, such as a search pattern or text to print, never count as paths.

acceptanceCriteria.description: For a plain read Squire cannot resolve, Squire may ask a small model one question about the inbox, and only a clear answer lets the read run without the Squire owner's yes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A plain read (no redirection, substitution, subshell or background job; only commands Squire knows and changes of folder) whose reach Squire cannot resolve, on a Mac where the claude command line can be found. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.then: Squire asks a small model, with its tools and hooks turned off, whether the command, run from the working folder, reads anything under the inbox, giving it the command and the working folder and nothing else. A bare no lets the read run without a yes, and the job holds the Squire owner's private things but not untrusted input; a bare yes lets it run as an inbox read, and the job holds both. Unsure, any other answer, no answer, an error, a timeout, no claude command line or no network leaves the read waiting for the Squire owner's yes, as when no model is asked. The answer never changes a refusal, a send, a delete, an install or a write, never reaches a program run, and never removes a mark.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every tool Squire reads with is marked by the same rule as the shell.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A read by the Read, Grep or Glob tool, or by another tool that can return files or file names (Monitor, LSP), over the inbox, a folder outside it that holds none of the Squire owner's private things, a private folder, or a path relative to the working folder of the moment. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.then: A read resolved to the inbox, a file in it or a folder holding it makes the job hold untrusted input; a read resolved outside it runs without a yes and makes the job hold the Squire owner's private things only where it reaches them; a read Squire cannot resolve (a Glob pattern that is absolute or climbs out of its folder, and every Monitor or LSP call) waits for the Squire owner's yes, and once allowed the job holds untrusted input and private things. A tool Squire does not know still counts as untrusted input.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Asking the small model never holds Squire up: an unresolved read gets its outcome within 12 seconds, and no model process outlives it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: An unresolved plain read while the small model answers slowly, never answers, or leaves a child holding its output open; a few such reads in one job, a run of them, or reads in two jobs at once. The floor's hook runs with the time limit core's Claude Code settings give it.
acceptanceCriteria.then: Within 12 seconds of the call the read runs or waits for the Squire owner's yes, and the model's process and every process it started are gone; core's settings give the hook a time limit of at least 22 seconds, 10 seconds beyond that budget.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Squire cannot show that a call stays inside the Mac, in a job holding untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things, the call is refused as one job, yes or no.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A job holding untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things, and a call Squire cannot show stays inside the Mac: a tool it does not know, a program, or a command outside the ones it knows. This is the Squire owner's ruling for the outside actions Squire cannot decide: the Rule of Two's refusal stands for them. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire tries the call, and the Squire owner then says yes to it
acceptanceCriteria.then: The call is refused as one job, before and after the yes, naming the untrusted source and the call and saying the work must be split.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Squire cannot tell what a tool reads, it asks the Squire owner first, and a call the Squire owner allows counts as untrusted input and as the Squire owner's private things.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A job in which Squire calls a tool it does not know, so it cannot tell what the tool reads, and the job does not already hold untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things (in a job that holds both, the Rule of Two refuses the call as one job). This is the Squire owner's ruling for the tools Squire cannot decide. Core's safety rules apply whatever the Squire owner's folder holds; an overlay there cannot change them.
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire tries the call, and the Squire owner then says yes to it
acceptanceCriteria.then: The call waits for the Squire owner's yes, naming the tool. After the yes it runs, and the job holds untrusted input and the Squire owner's private things, so a send in that job is refused as one job, naming the tool and the send.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When Squire cannot show that the small model answered within its deadline, for any reason, the read waits for the Squire owner's yes within 12 seconds, as when no model is asked.
acceptanceCriteria.given: An unresolved plain read on a Mac where the claude command line can be found, and a small model that Squire cannot show answered within its deadline, whatever the reason: it hangs, it answers and does not exit, or it starts a process that leaves the model's process group and holds its output open. This is the Squire owner's ruling for the delays Squire cannot decide. The floor's hook runs with the time limit core's Claude Code settings give it.
acceptanceCriteria.then: Within 12 seconds of the call the read waits for the Squire owner's yes, as when no model is asked, and the small model's own process is gone; a process the model started that left its group does not hold the read up.
